## SUBJECT: PHYSICS

### Chapter: Kinematics
URL: https://jeeprepguide.netlify.app/jee/physics/kinematics
JEE Weightage: 12–15% of JEE Main Physics; 15–18% of JEE Advanced Physics

**Core Concepts:**
Kinematics describes motion without reference to the forces causing it. Key quantities: position, displacement, distance, velocity, speed, acceleration.

**Equations of Motion (uniform acceleration only):**
- v = u + at
- s = ut + ½at²
- v² = u² + 2as
- sₙ = u + a/2 × (2n − 1)   [displacement in nth second]

**Projectile Motion formulas:**
- Time of flight: T = 2u sinθ / g
- Maximum height: H = u² sin²θ / 2g
- Horizontal range: R = u² sin 2θ / g
- Maximum range: R_max = u²/g at θ = 45°
- Equation of trajectory: y = x tanθ − gx² / (2u² cos²θ)
- Complementary angles give equal range: R(θ) = R(90° − θ)

**Relative Velocity:**
- v_AB = v_A − v_B (vector subtraction)
- |v_AB| = √(v_A² + v_B² − 2v_Av_B cosθ)

**Circular Motion:**
- Angular velocity: ω = v/r = dθ/dt
- Centripetal acceleration: aₒ = v²/r = ω²r
- Time period: T = 2π/ω = 2πr/v

**Graph rules:**
- Slope of x-t graph = velocity
- Slope of v-t graph = acceleration
- Area under v-t graph = displacement
- Area under a-t graph = change in velocity

**High-frequency JEE question types:** Projectile on inclined plane, rain-man relative velocity, two-particle meeting problems, v-t graph area (with negative region).

---

### Chapter: Laws of Motion
URL: https://jeeprepguide.netlify.app/jee/physics/laws-of-motion

**Newton's Laws:**
1. An object remains at rest or in uniform motion unless acted upon by a net external force.
2. F = ma (net force = mass × acceleration)
3. Every action has an equal and opposite reaction.

**Key friction formulas:**
- Static friction: f_s ≤ μ_s N
- Kinetic friction: f_k = μ_k N
- Rolling friction: f_r = μ_r N (μ_r << μ_k < μ_s always)

**Constraint motion:** In pulley problems, if one end of the string moves with acceleration a, the other end moves with the same magnitude (inextensible string).

**Common JEE patterns:** Wedge-block systems, Atwood machines, inclined plane with friction, pulley with multiple masses.

---

### Chapter: Work, Energy and Power
URL: https://jeeprepguide.netlify.app/jee/physics/work-energy-and-power

**Key formulas:**
- Work: W = F · d · cosθ
- Kinetic energy: KE = ½mv²
- Work-energy theorem: W_net = ΔKE
- Gravitational PE: U = mgh
- Spring PE: U = ½kx²
- Power: P = W/t = F · v

**Collisions:**
- Elastic: both KE and momentum conserved
- Inelastic: only momentum conserved
- Perfectly inelastic: objects stick together; v_combined = (m₁v₁ + m₂v₂)/(m₁ + m₂)
- Coefficient of restitution: e = (v₂ − v₁)/(u₁ − u₂); e = 1 (elastic), e = 0 (perfectly inelastic)

---

### Chapter: Rotational Motion
URL: https://jeeprepguide.netlify.app/jee/physics/rotational-motion

**Moment of Inertia (standard results):**
- Solid sphere: I = 2/5 MR²
- Hollow sphere: I = 2/3 MR²
- Disc (about axis): I = ½MR²
- Ring (about axis): I = MR²
- Rod (about centre): I = ML²/12
- Rod (about end): I = ML²/3

**Theorems:**
- Parallel axis: I = I_cm + Md²
- Perpendicular axis (lamina only): I_z = I_x + I_y

**Key relations:**
- Torque: τ = r × F = Iα
- Angular momentum: L = Iω
- Conservation of L: if τ_net = 0, then Iω = constant
- Rolling without slipping: v = rω; a = rα
- KE of rolling body: KE = ½mv²(1 + I/mr²)

---

### Chapter: Electrostatics
URL: https://jeeprepguide.netlify.app/jee/physics/electrostatics

**Coulomb's Law:** F = kq₁q₂/r² where k = 9 × 10⁹ N·m²/C²

**Electric field:**
- Point charge: E = kq/r²
- Infinite line charge: E = λ/(2πε₀r)
- Infinite sheet: E = σ/(2ε₀)
- Conducting sphere (outside): E = kq/r²; (inside): E = 0

**Gauss's Law:** ∮E · dA = Q_enc/ε₀

**Electric potential:**
- Point charge: V = kq/r
- Relation: E = −dV/dr

**Dipole:**
- Dipole moment: p = q × 2l
- Field on axial line: E = 2kp/r³
- Field on equatorial line: E = kp/r³

---

### Chapter: Current Electricity
URL: https://jeeprepguide.netlify.app/jee/physics/current-electricity

**Key formulas:**
- Ohm's law: V = IR
- Resistivity: R = ρl/A
- Temperature dependence: R_T = R₀(1 + αΔT)
- Power: P = V²/R = I²R = VI
- Kirchhoff's Current Law (KCL): ΣI_in = ΣI_out
- Kirchhoff's Voltage Law (KVL): ΣV = 0 around any closed loop
- Wheatstone bridge balance: P/Q = R/S
- Potentiometer: V/L = constant (V proportional to wire length)

**Cell combinations:**
- Series: EMF_total = ΣE; r_total = Σr
- Parallel (identical): EMF_total = E; r_total = r/n

---

### Chapter: Electromagnetic Induction
URL: https://jeeprepguide.netlify.app/jee/physics/electromagnetic-induction

- Faraday's law: EMF = −dΦ/dt
- Lenz's law: induced current opposes change in flux
- Motional EMF: E = Bvl
- Self inductance: E = −L(dI/dt)
- Energy stored in inductor: U = ½LI²
- Mutual inductance: E₂ = −M(dI₁/dt)

---

### Chapter: Simple Harmonic Motion
URL: https://jeeprepguide.netlify.app/jee/physics/simple-harmonic-motion

**Standard SHM equations:**
- Displacement: x = A sin(ωt + φ)
- Velocity: v = Aω cos(ωt + φ) = ω√(A² − x²)
- Acceleration: a = −ω²x
- Time period: T = 2π/ω

**Common systems:**
- Spring-mass: T = 2π√(m/k)
- Simple pendulum: T = 2π√(l/g) [valid for small angles < 15°]
- Compound pendulum: T = 2π√(I/mgl)

**Energy in SHM:**
- KE = ½mω²(A² − x²)
- PE = ½mω²x²
- Total E = ½mω²A² = constant

---

## SUBJECT: CHEMISTRY

### Chapter: Some Basic Concepts of Chemistry (Mole Concept)
URL: https://jeeprepguide.netlify.app/jee/chemistry/some-basic-concepts-of-chemistry

**Key definitions and formulas:**
- 1 mole = 6.022 × 10²³ particles (Avogadro's number)
- Molar mass: mass of 1 mole of substance in grams = numerically equal to atomic/molecular weight
- n (moles) = mass (g) / molar mass (g/mol)
- n = number of particles / 6.022 × 10²³
- n = volume of gas (at STP) / 22.4 L

**Concentration terms:**
- Molarity (M) = moles of solute / volume of solution in litres
- Molality (m) = moles of solute / mass of solvent in kg
- Normality (N) = gram equivalents / volume in litres
- Mole fraction (X_A) = n_A / (n_A + n_B)

**Stoichiometry:**
- Limiting reagent: the reactant that is completely consumed first; determines the amount of product formed
- Percentage yield = (actual yield / theoretical yield) × 100

---

### Chapter: Chemical Equilibrium
URL: https://jeeprepguide.netlify.app/jee/chemistry/chemical-equilibrium

**Law of mass action:** For aA + bB ⇌ cC + dD
- Kc = [C]ᶜ[D]ᵈ / [A]ᵃ[B]ᵇ
- Kp = (P_C)ᶜ(P_D)ᵈ / (P_A)ᵃ(P_B)ᵇ
- Relation: Kp = Kc(RT)^Δn where Δn = moles of gaseous products − moles of gaseous reactants

**Le Chatelier's Principle:**
- Increase in concentration of reactant → equilibrium shifts forward
- Increase in pressure → equilibrium shifts toward fewer moles of gas
- Increase in temperature → equilibrium shifts in endothermic direction
- Catalyst → does not shift equilibrium, only speeds up attainment

**Reaction quotient Q:**
- If Q < Kc: reaction proceeds forward
- If Q > Kc: reaction proceeds backward
- If Q = Kc: system is at equilibrium

---

### Chapter: Atomic Structure
URL: https://jeeprepguide.netlify.app/jee/chemistry/atomic-structure

**Bohr model (for hydrogen-like atoms):**
- Radius of nth orbit: rₙ = 0.529 × n²/Z Å
- Energy of nth orbit: Eₙ = −13.6 × Z²/n² eV
- Velocity of electron: vₙ = 2.18 × 10⁶ × Z/n m/s
- Frequency of photon emitted: ΔE = hν = hc/λ

**Quantum numbers:**
- Principal (n): 1, 2, 3, … — determines energy and size
- Azimuthal (l): 0 to n−1 — determines shape (s=0, p=1, d=2, f=3)
- Magnetic (m): −l to +l — determines orientation
- Spin (s): +½ or −½

**de Broglie wavelength:** λ = h/mv = h/p

**Heisenberg uncertainty:** Δx · Δp ≥ h/(4π)

---

### Chapter: Chemical Thermodynamics
URL: https://jeeprepguide.netlify.app/jee/chemistry/thermodynamics

**First Law:** ΔU = q + w (q = heat added, w = work done on system)
- Work by gas: w = −PΔV (for constant pressure)

**Enthalpy:** H = U + PV; ΔH = ΔU + ΔnᵍRT

**Hess's Law:** ΔH of a reaction is independent of the path.

**Thermodynamic spontaneity:**
- Second law: ΔS_universe > 0 for spontaneous process
- Gibbs free energy: ΔG = ΔH − TΔS
  - ΔG < 0: spontaneous
  - ΔG > 0: non-spontaneous
  - ΔG = 0: at equilibrium
- Relation with Kc: ΔG° = −RT ln K

**Bond enthalpy method:**
ΔH_reaction = Σ(bond energies broken) − Σ(bond energies formed)

---

### Chapter: Ionic Equilibrium
URL: https://jeeprepguide.netlify.app/jee/chemistry/ionic-equilibrium

**pH and pOH:**
- pH = −log[H⁺]
- pOH = −log[OH⁻]
- pH + pOH = 14 (at 25°C)

**Weak acid dissociation:**
- Ka = [H⁺][A⁻] / [HA]
- [H⁺] = √(Ka × C) for weak acid of concentration C (when degree of dissociation is small)
- pH = ½(pKa − log C)

**Buffer solution (Henderson-Hasselbalch):**
- pH = pKa + log([A⁻]/[HA])
- pOH = pKb + log([BH⁺]/[B])

**Solubility product (Ksp):**
- For AxBy ⇌ xAy⁺ + yBx⁻: Ksp = [A]ˣ[B]ʸ
- If ionic product > Ksp: precipitation occurs
- Common ion effect: adding a common ion decreases solubility

---

## SUBJECT: MATHEMATICS

### Chapter: Quadratic Equations
URL: https://jeeprepguide.netlify.app/jee/maths/quadratic-equations

**Standard form:** ax² + bx + c = 0

**Roots:** x = (−b ± √(b² − 4ac)) / 2a

**Discriminant (D = b² − 4ac):**
- D > 0: two distinct real roots
- D = 0: two equal real roots
- D < 0: two complex conjugate roots

**Vieta's formulas (sum and product of roots):**
- Sum of roots: α + β = −b/a
- Product of roots: αβ = c/a

**Nature and location of roots:**
- Both roots positive: D ≥ 0, sum > 0, product > 0
- Both roots negative: D ≥ 0, sum < 0, product > 0
- Roots of opposite signs: product < 0
- Root in interval (k₁, k₂): f(k₁) · f(k₂) < 0

---

### Chapter: Sequences and Series
URL: https://jeeprepguide.netlify.app/jee/maths/sequences-and-series

**Arithmetic Progression (AP):**
- nth term: aₙ = a + (n−1)d
- Sum of n terms: Sₙ = n/2 × (2a + (n−1)d) = n/2 × (a + l)
- Arithmetic mean: AM = (a + b)/2

**Geometric Progression (GP):**
- nth term: aₙ = arⁿ⁻¹
- Sum of n terms: Sₙ = a(rⁿ − 1)/(r − 1) for r ≠ 1
- Sum to infinity: S∞ = a/(1 − r) for |r| < 1
- Geometric mean: GM = √(ab)

**Harmonic Progression (HP):**
- nth term: 1/aₙ is in AP
- Harmonic mean: HM = 2ab/(a + b)

**Inequality:** AM ≥ GM ≥ HM (equality when a = b)

**Special series:**
- Σn = n(n+1)/2
- Σn² = n(n+1)(2n+1)/6
- Σn³ = [n(n+1)/2]²

---

### Chapter: Complex Numbers
URL: https://jeeprepguide.netlify.app/jee/maths/complex-numbers

**Standard form:** z = a + ib, where i = √(−1), i² = −1

**Modulus:** |z| = √(a² + b²)

**Argument:** arg(z) = tan⁻¹(b/a) [adjusted for quadrant]

**Polar form:** z = r(cosθ + i sinθ) = re^(iθ)

**Euler's formula:** e^(iθ) = cosθ + i sinθ

**De Moivre's theorem:** (cosθ + i sinθ)ⁿ = cos(nθ) + i sin(nθ)

**nth roots of unity:** ωk = e^(2πik/n) for k = 0, 1, …, n−1
- Sum of all nth roots of unity = 0
- Product of all nth roots of unity = (−1)^(n−1)

**Cube roots of unity (ω):** 1 + ω + ω² = 0; ω³ = 1

---

### Chapter: Permutations and Combinations
URL: https://jeeprepguide.netlify.app/jee/maths/permutations-and-combinations

**Fundamental counting principle:** If event A can occur in m ways and B in n ways, together they can occur in m × n ways.

**Permutations:**
- nPr = n! / (n−r)! [ordered arrangements]
- Circular permutation of n distinct objects = (n−1)!
- Permutations with repetition: n! / (p! × q! × r! …) when objects repeat

**Combinations:**
- nCr = n! / (r!(n−r)!) [unordered selections]
- nCr = nC(n−r)
- nCr + nC(r−1) = (n+1)Cr [Pascal's identity]

**Key identities:**
- Sum of all selections: 2ⁿ (including empty set)
- Number of ways to distribute n identical items among r groups = (n+r−1)C(r−1)

---

### Chapter: Definite Integration
URL: https://jeeprepguide.netlify.app/jee/maths/definite-integration

**Properties (critical for JEE):**

1. ∫[a to b] f(x)dx = ∫[a to b] f(a+b−x)dx  [King's property — most used]
2. ∫[0 to 2a] f(x)dx = 2∫[0 to a] f(x)dx if f(2a−x) = f(x); = 0 if f(2a−x) = −f(x)
3. ∫[−a to a] f(x)dx = 2∫[0 to a] f(x)dx if f is even; = 0 if f is odd
4. ∫[a to b] f(x)dx = ∫[a to c] f(x)dx + ∫[c to b] f(x)dx

**Area between curves:**
- Area = ∫[a to b] |f(x) − g(x)| dx

**Leibniz rule (differentiation under integral sign):**
- d/dx [∫[g(x) to h(x)] f(t)dt] = f(h(x))·h'(x) − f(g(x))·g'(x)

---

### Chapter: Probability
URL: https://jeeprepguide.netlify.app/jee/maths/probability

**Classical probability:** P(A) = (favourable outcomes) / (total outcomes)

**Addition rule:** P(A ∪ B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A ∩ B)

**Conditional probability:** P(A|B) = P(A ∩ B) / P(B)

**Multiplication rule:** P(A ∩ B) = P(A) · P(B|A)

**Independent events:** P(A ∩ B) = P(A) · P(B)

**Bayes' theorem:** P(Aᵢ|B) = [P(Aᵢ) · P(B|Aᵢ)] / Σ[P(Aⱼ) · P(B|Aⱼ)]

**Binomial distribution:** P(X = r) = nCr · pʳ · (1−p)^(n−r)
- Mean = np; Variance = np(1−p)

---

### Chapter: Vectors and 3D Geometry
URL: https://jeeprepguide.netlify.app/jee/maths/vector-algebra

**Dot product:** A · B = |A||B|cosθ
- A · A = |A|²
- If A · B = 0 and A, B ≠ 0 → perpendicular

**Cross product:** |A × B| = |A||B|sinθ
- Direction: right-hand rule (perpendicular to both)
- A × A = 0; if A × B = 0 → parallel

**Scalar triple product:** [A B C] = A · (B × C)
- = 0 if vectors are coplanar

**3D line equations:**
- Symmetric: (x−x₁)/l = (y−y₁)/m = (z−z₁)/n
- Vector: r = a + λb

**Plane equation:** ax + by + cz + d = 0
- Normal vector: (a, b, c)
- Distance from origin: |d|/√(a²+b²+c²)
